questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:
questions.explanation: You can see a trailer skid earliest in your mirrors. Watch your mirrors to see if the trailer is moving off course.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be closest to the cab?
questions.explanation: Put the heaviest loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the back.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle:

options.text: Will not make a difference in braking.
Will provide better control when braking.
Will likely cause the air brakes to break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will provide better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even with anti-lock brakes on just one axle, you will have better braking control than without any anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of a rollover, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo close to the ground to lower rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often what color?
questions.explanation: Match glad hands by color to couple them correctly. Service lines are usually blue. Emergency lines are usually red.

questions.question: When backing your tractor to couple with a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer during coupling.

questions.question: To help prevent rollovers, you should:

options.text: Keep the load at the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Keep cargo low and centered. Drive slowly through curves and corners to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle turns a corner:

options.text: Make the turn as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should go over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. It is more pronounced on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: Starting in what year were new trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ skill than operating single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly can cause:

options.text: A whip-like effect that can cause the vehicle to roll over.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A whip-like effect that can cause the vehicle to roll over.
questions.explanation: When you change lanes too quickly with a trailer, the rear of the vehicle swings out sharply. This whip-like motion can cause the vehicle to roll over.

questions.question: Set the trailer air supply control to "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you drive. Pull the air supply control to the emergency position. Move forward slightly. The trailer should not move. If it does, the emergency brakes are not working.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows the wheels to lock up.
It stops the wheels from locking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. When ABS detects that the wheels are about to lock up, it reduces brake pressure to keep the wheels turning.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, you should:

options.text: Move back and forth side to side while backing.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back straight, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Disconnecting air lines and listening for air escaping.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Wait for air pressure to build up. Send air to the emergency and service brake lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching all trailers.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:
questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. If the trailer is too low, the nose may be damaged. If the trailer is too high, it may not connect properly.

questions.question: If the trailer spring brakes do not release when you push the air supply control, you should:

options.text: Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and back on.

questions.explanation: Before driving, all equipment must work properly. If the trailer spring brakes do not release, make sure the air line connections are tight and properly sealed.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will lose brakes if the air supply leaks. This means:

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks out, there are no brakes to stop the trailer. The wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: To test the trailer service brakes, you should:

options.text: Move forward slowly and press the brake pedal.
Back up slowly and use the hand control.
Back up slowly and press the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and use the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and use the hand control.
questions.explanation: Make sure the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly. Use the hand control to apply the brakes. You should feel the trailer brakes activate if they are working.
